title: A failing `from tools.memory_tool import ...` in agent_init._init_memory leaves mem_config unbound and silently drops the configured external memory provider

candidates.author: Wenfengcheng
candidates.has_tests: yes: 3 test functions / 10 cases (public AIAgent ctor, core/absent/malformed provider boundaries, disk-installed MemoryProvider through real config.yaml)
candidates.approach: Provider selection reads _cfg_dict(_agent_cfg, 'memory').get('provider', '') instead of the built-in block's local mem_config. Same normalization as get_builtin_memory_config on the success path; the built-in store stays optional and silent. 'Part of #125919' (config-load diagnostics left to #125960). Labels type/bug, comp/agent, comp/plugins, tool/memory, P3, area/memory.

candidates.author: richardclawbot
candidates.merges_clean_on_pinned_main: false: conflicts in agent/agent_init.py and agent/memory_manager.py (written against the pre-_init_memory init_agent layout)
candidates.approach: Feature: honor memory.external_prefetch_timeout. Hoists mem_config = _agent_cfg.get('memory', {}) above the built-in try as a side effect, which would also bind it on import failure (raw section, so a malformed section has the same 'str'.get problem as fork #30). Does not reference #125919. Not A/B'd (conflicting, different defect).

candidates.author: natehale
candidates.approach: Feature: per-job cron external memory provider modes (needs-decision). Initializes mem_config = {} before the built-in block as a side effect. Not A/B'd (conflicting, design-gated feature).

regression_test.source: #126106's tests/agent/test_memory_bootstrap_independence.py, unchanged (byte-identical to the previous run's leftover copy)
regression_test.contract: When `from tools.memory_tool import ...` fails inside _init_memory, a configured external provider is still loaded, initialized with the session id and its tools injected (public AIAgent ctor and a disk-installed provider via config.yaml), while skip_memory still loads nothing. Absent, blank, core or malformed provider settings load no provider and log no 'Memory provider plugin init failed'.

main.detail: 7 failed / 3 passed. Public ctor with skip_memory=False plus import failure: 'built-in import disabled the external provider' (_memory_manager is None). Disk provider: manager None. All 5 core/absent/malformed cases log "Memory provider plugin init failed: cannot access local variable 'mem_config' where it is not associated with a value".

fork#30 (kvnloo, reference, not an upstr.detail: 1 failed / 9 passed. 381e59256b conflicts on main (init_agent was split into _init_memory with suppress()), so its production hunk was hand-ported (fork30-ported-onto-main.diff, +7/-1: raw default mem_config = _agent_cfg.get('memory', {}) before the block, plus the once-per-process 'Built-in memory store unavailable' warning). [malformed] fails: the raw default is the string 'malformed', so the import-failure path logs "Memory provider plugin init failed: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'".

87028.detail: CONFLICTING on main (agent/agent_init.py, agent/memory_manager.py). Same raw-section hoist as fork #30, as a side effect of a prefetch-timeout feature.

18565.detail: CONFLICTING on main (11 files). Needs-decision cron feature; mem_config = {} default is a side effect.

negative_control.detail: On main + #126106 with its line reverted to mem_config.get('provider', '') if mem_config else '': 7 failed / 3 passed, identical to main.

adjacent_tests.result: Main: 86 passed, 0 failed. Main + #126106: 96 passed, 0 failed (86 + its 10). kvnloo fork #30's own tests/run_agent/test_mem_config_unbound_init.py is stale (patches run_agent.get_tool_definitions, which no longer exists): 0/3 on main and on #126106.

carrier.author: Wenfengcheng <30426178+Wenfengcheng@users.noreply.github.com>
carrier.why: The only upstream PR aimed at this defect. It is a 3-line production change that reuses the existing _cfg_dict normalization, so it is correct on malformed sections where the raw-section hoist (fork #30, #87028) is not. Its test drives the public AIAgent constructor and a real disk-installed provider, it merges clean and GitHub reports MERGEABLE. #87028 and #18565 fix it only as a side effect of conflicting feature PRs.

notes: (1) Partial fix by design: #126106 is 'Part of #125919'. The config-load warning half is #125960 (YS-OH-CORE, MERGEABLE), which touches a different hunk (init_agent's load_config_readonly fallback) and composes with #126106 without a textual conflict (not merged together here). After both, the remaining silent case in #125919 is the built-in store itself: with tools.memory_tool unimportable, agent._memory_store stays None with no log at any level. (2) kvnloo fork #30's only distinct content is a once-per-process WARNING 'Built-in memory store unavailable: %s' replacing that silent suppress(). It is a separate diagnostic contract, adjacent to #125960 (which deliberately omits exception text because config errors can carry secrets) and #43313. Offer it as a review suggestion on #126106 or #125960, not as a fold-in. (3) Fork #30's raw-section default (and #87028's identical hoist) mishandles memory: <non-dict> on the import-failure path; #126106 does not. (4) Fork-side: close kvnloo/hermes-agent#30 after the carrier merges. (5) The previous run's leftover memcfg diff was #126106 merged as-is; everything was re-run here on 298a01c7. Refs pinned: refs/w2/pr/{126106,87028,18565}, refs/w2/fork/30 (hand-port, reference only). No tripwire hits.
